+// Best-effort Flashscore lineup scraper fallback.
+// Flashscore HTML structure may change; this helper tries a few heuristics.
+export async function fetchFlashscoreLineups(

+  awayName: string,
+  date?: string
+) {

+
+  // Create a naive slug from team names
+  const slugCandidates = []
+  const normalize = (s: string) =>
+    s
+      .toLowerCase()
+      .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
+      .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")
+
+  slugCandidates.push(`${normalize(homeName)}-${normalize(awayName)}`)
+  slugCandidates.push(`${normalize(awayName)}-${normalize(homeName)}`)
+
+  for (const slug of slugCandidates) {
+    const urls = [
+      `https://www.flashscore.com/match/${slug}/#match-lineups`,
+      `https://www.flashscore.com/match/${slug}/`,
+      `https://m.flashscore.com/match/${slug}/`,

+        })
+

+        const nameRegex = /([A-Z][a-z]+\s[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s[A-Z][a-z]+)?)/g
+        const matches = Array.from(new Set((html.match(nameRegex) || []).slice(0, 40)))

Short answer: you can start charging customers as soon as you have authentication, a Stripe account + webhook handling, a paid feature gated behind subscriptions, and a live deployment — realistically 2–6 weeks depending on scope.

Recommended minimal path to revenue (with rough times):
- Week 0–1: Add auth (`NextAuth`/Clerk) + user/accounts (2–5 days).  
- Week 1: Integrate Stripe (products/plans, checkout, webhooks) + subscription gating (3–7 days).  
- Week 2: Deploy to production (Vercel), connect domain, add SSL and webhooks (1–3 days).  
- Week 2–3: Create pricing page, billing UI, legal pages (TOS/Privacy), email for invoices (2–5 days).  
- Week 3–4: QA, analytics, add basic support flow and onboarding; soft-launch to first customers.

Minimum paid feature suggestions (pick one to monetize immediately):
- API access tier (signals/lineups) with rate limits.
- Premium dashboard with historical analytics and export.
- Alerts/email delivery of signals for subscribers.

Must-haves before charging:
- Stripe account + business verification and bank details.
- Terms of service & privacy policy pages.
- Billing webhooks (to update user subscription state).
- Basic invoices/receipt emails.
- Data/license compliance: scraping Flashscore or Soccerwiki may breach terms — prefer licensing or a proxy with permission.

Immediate next step I can do now (pick one):
- "Integrate Stripe checkout + webhooks" (I will implement backend routes and example UI).

If you created/linked your account with Google/GitHub SSO, a password reset won’t help — use the “Sign in with Google” / SSO button instead (I see a Google sign-in page open).  

Quick checklist — try these in order:
- If you normally click “Sign in with Google” or an organization SSO, use that flow (password reset is irrelevant).  
- Open an incognito/private window and try signing in (avoids cookie/extension problems).  
- Ensure you used the exact email on the account and check spam/junk for the reset link; request a new reset and use the most recent email (links expire).  
- If 2FA is enabled, use your authenticator app or recovery codes. Do NOT share codes or passwords here.  
- If you still see an error, try a different device/network (VPNs/proxies sometimes block).  
- If none of that works, start GitHub account recovery via their docs and support — include proof (email, recent repo names, billing info):

  - Contact/support form: https://support.github.com/contact

If you want, I can:
- Open the Google sign-in page (already open) so you can complete OAuth, or
- Open the password reset page again, or
- Capture a screenshot of the error you see so I can advise precisely.

Getting this SaaS live — quick deploy checklist

1) Required environment variables

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` — e.g. https://yourdomain.com
- `API_FOOTBALL_KEY` — (optional) API‑Sports key
- `SOCCERWIKI_API_URL` — optional proxy for Soccerwiki ratings
- Clerk: `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`
- Supabase: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (or anon for limited use)
- Stripe: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

2) Database (Supabase)

- Apply migration file:
  ```
  psql "postgresql://<DB_USER>:<DB_PASS>@<DB_HOST>:<DB_PORT>/<DB_NAME>" -f db/migrations/001_create_billing_tables.sql
  psql "postgresql://<DB_USER>:<DB_PASS>@<DB_HOST>:<DB_PORT>/<DB_NAME>" -f db/seeds/001_seed_sample.sql
  ```
- Or use Supabase UI: SQL Editor → run migration and seed SQL.

3) Stripe

- Create a Product and Price (recurring). Copy the `priceId` into Vercel env as `NEXT_PUBLIC_TEST_PRICE_ID` (for local dev also set in `.env.local`).
- Configure a webhook in Stripe dashboard pointing to `https://<YOUR_DOMAIN>/api/stripe/webhook` and copy the Webhook Signing Secret into `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

4) Clerk

- Create a Clerk app and add the allowed origin(s) including the dev URL (http://localhost:3000) and your production domain.
- Set Clerk env vars in Vercel.

5) Deploy (Vercel recommended)

- Push changes to GitHub, connect repository in Vercel, set the environment variables in the Vercel dashboard, and deploy.

6) Test flow

- Sign up via `/sign-in` (Clerk). Visit `/pricing` → Subscribe → complete checkout. Confirm Stripe webhook writes to Supabase.

7) Notes & next steps

- For production reliability add caching for Soccerwiki requests, a job/worker for scraping Flashscore if needed, and monitor Stripe webhook retries.
- Add legal pages and billing email templates before public launch.

+  psql "postgresql://<DB_USER>:<DB_PASS>@<DB_HOST>:<DB_PORT>/<DB_NAME>" -f db/seeds/001_seed_sample.sql

+

+7) Notes & next steps
+
+- For production reliability add caching for Soccerwiki requests, a job/worker for scraping Flashscore if needed, and monitor Stripe webhook retries.

+
